Definition: Whether the country has an operational Internet Exchange Point (IXP) and its maturity. IXPs enable local internet traffic to be exchanged domestically rather than being routed internationally, reducing latency, costs, and dependence on foreign infrastructure. Critical for local digital ecosystem development.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed: SEY-IX (AS37707), Seychelles' only IXP, launched 2015 and remains active (AFRINIC record last updated Feb 2025) but shows only one visible public peer (AS6517 LakeNetworks) on bgp.he.net, consistent with 'single IXP with limited participation'. Value Code 3 stands.

Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)
Comments: No local hyperscale; distant regions available (AWS Cape Town, Azure/GC nearby) ([AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/global-infrastructure/regions_az/))
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Latency estimates put Seychelles-to-Johannesburg (nearest AWS/Azure region) at roughly 77-84ms, under the 100ms threshold used to distinguish 'served remotely from distant regions' (Code 2) from 'regional cloud availability zone nearby' (Code 3); AWS's af-south-1 (Cape Town) is marketed as the Sub-Saharan Africa regional zone. Revised upward to Code 3, but figures are modelled estimates rather than direct Seychelles measurements — recommend human review to confirm with an actual Seychelles-based latency test.
